name: Cameroon
summary: Cameroon is ranked the world's most neglected displacement crisis by NRC in 2025. Three overlapping emergencies — the Anglophone separatist war, Boko Haram in the Far North, and CAR refugee spillover — displace over 844,000 people. Security incidents nearly doubled in 2024, with 7,035 incidents recorded, yet the crisis generated only 28,800 media articles — 15 times fewer than Ukraine.
context:
Cameroon hosts three simultaneous humanitarian crises that have received almost no international attention despite their combined scale and severity. In the Northwest and Southwest regions, a separatist conflict between Anglophone armed groups (known collectively as 'Ambazonia' forces) and Cameroonian government security forces has displaced hundreds of thousands and created a crisis characterized by attacks on civilians, school closures, and a systematic breakdown of services in English-speaking areas.

In the Far North region bordering Nigeria and Chad, Boko Haram and ISWAP conduct regular attacks on villages, markets, and aid workers, maintaining a persistent state of insecurity for lakeside communities. Over 300,000 people are displaced in this region alone.

In the East, Cameroon hosts over 300,000 refugees from the Central African Republic, straining already limited local resources in one of the most underdeveloped parts of the country.

The NRC ranked Cameroon the world's most neglected displacement crisis in 2025, citing the extraordinary gap between scale and coverage. Only 28,800 media articles were published about Cameroon's crisis in all of 2024 — compared to over 400,000 for Ukraine. Security incidents nearly doubled from 2023 to 2024, rising to 7,035 documented incidents. Yet the humanitarian response remains chronically underfunded.

Over 3.3 million people need humanitarian assistance. The Anglophone crisis in particular has been characterized by a near-complete absence of international pressure despite documented atrocities by both government forces and armed separatist groups.

donate.name: Norwegian Refugee Council
donate.description: Delivering legal aid, education, shelter, and emergency assistance to displaced Cameroonians across all three crisis zones.

donate.name: UNFPA Cameroon
donate.description: Providing sexual and reproductive health services to displaced women and girls in Cameroon's crisis-affected regions.

donate.name: International Crisis Group
donate.description: Researching and advocating for political solutions to Cameroon's overlapping crises, particularly the Anglophone conflict.

awareness: Share that NRC ranked Cameroon the world's most neglected displacement crisis in 2025 — by definition, this is a crisis the world is not paying attention to
Highlight the media gap: 28,800 articles about Cameroon vs 400,000+ about Ukraine in 2024 — invisibility has life-and-death consequences
Amplify Anglophone Cameroonian voices documenting the separatist conflict, which involves atrocities on both sides with no accountability
Raise awareness about the triple crisis structure — three separate emergencies in one country, each capable of independently qualifying as a major crisis
Support Cameroonian civil society organizations and diaspora groups working toward dialogue and accountability
political: Urge your government to pressure Cameroon for a political dialogue process in the Anglophone regions — the conflict cannot be solved militarily
Push for increased humanitarian funding for Cameroon's response — chronic underfunding is directly killing people
Advocate for independent investigations into atrocities in the Northwest and Southwest — both government forces and separatist groups have committed abuses
Support regional initiatives to address cross-border dynamics with Nigeria (Boko Haram) and CAR (refugee flows)
Demand that Cameroon allow unimpeded access for humanitarian organizations to all conflict-affected regions
